notes.title: We’re celebrating three years of Citizen Sleeper!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238001/b2c5cb56cab097a0bc06283c373189730af37383.jpg[/img]
It’s been three years since Citizen Sleeper first invited us into its hauntingly beautiful world of drifting space stations, corporate collapse, and the desperate hope of those who try to survive between the cracks. 🔺

Now, with over 2,000,000 players across the critically acclaimed original and sequel, Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector, it’s time to celebrate everything the Citizen Sleeper universe has become. 🎉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238001/49c5cf9c0fb4e56d37ced304bd1596c40c699fb4.jpg[/img]
[b]The universe still grows[/b]
Fans of the series’ tabletop-inspired mechanics and lore-rich universe will not want to miss [url=https://jump-over-the-age.itch.io/citizen-sleeper-spindlejack]Spindlejack[/url], a brand new, free solo tabletop RPG from Gareth Damian Martin at Jump Over the Age. 🎲

Spindlejack puts you in the seat of a courier in Far Spindle - a familiar location for fans of Starward Vector. You must navigate the space station, earn cryo, and build your reputation so you can leave your mark on the courier scene - all while trying to survive with nothing but your airbike, your wits, and your dice. 🚲

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238001/f5950af0d55e5d156af67f17c9288228e345a9b0.jpg[/img]
[b]More players, more languages[/b]
In case you missed it, we announced last week that Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector will be getting full, high-quality localization into French, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese. Now even more Sleepers across the globe will be able to experience this unforgettable story about facing systemic issues, dealing with resource scarcity, building community while on the move, and facing the pull of your past - in their native language. 🌌

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238001/de0b487cd9a0f098503c52febebf8fc5e386281b.png[/img]
[b]This is the best time to jump in[/b]
If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to start your journey into the stars (or to bring a friend into the crew), Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector is at its lowest discount yet - 20% off - on Steam until 14 May! 🏷️

[b]Developer deep dive[/b]
Gareth Damian Martin will mark the occasion with a special anniversary stream on Steam, where they will do a deep dive into the Citizen Sleeper universe, giving unique developer insight into the lore that fans have come to know and love. 🤩

notes.title: Dice RPG Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector Has Taken to the Stars
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=ytLVnt3skzI;full][/previewyoutube]
It’s time, Sleeper! 🚀 The dice-driven RPG Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector is available for purchase today on Steam!

In Citizen Sleeper: Starward Vector, you play as an amnesiac android on the run from your corporate creators and the gang that seeks to control you for nefarious means. With bounty hunters hot in pursuit, you must contend with the growing threat of danger and your own malfunctioning body as you travel across the Starward Belt to survive its ramshackle set of habitats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238001/c847763332c1f1e6732481f3b9601eb68348a8c4.png[/img]
Secure (steal!) a ship, craft a crew, navigate relationships and take on challenging and high-risk contracts from the Belt’s many hubs to make ends meet. You will rely upon the roll of dice with the revolutionary and revised gameplay system from the original game, navigating skill checks and difficult decisions. Push your luck - literally - and strive for greater rewards at the risk of taking on stress, damaging the dice, and accruing game-changing glitches in your Sleeper’s already ailing system.

Chart a course across the Starward Belt’s vast and varied world and progress through this story-rich sci-fi setting, uncovering curious secrets, and checkered pasts that rival your Sleeper’s own. Beautifully decorated by famed comic book artist [url=https://www.instagram.com/blackysan]Guillaume Singelin[/url] and set to a soundtrack by the talented composer [url=https://www.amosroddy.com/]Amos Roddy[/url], you will experience a heartfelt and human tale about a character not wholly human themselves.

If you liked Citizen Sleeper, Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector dives deeper into its roleplaying roots with the dice of the original game taking on an even more important role. As an escaped Sleeper with a malfunctioning body, you commandeer a ship, find a crew, and take on contracts as you explore the Starward Belt. notes.title: Announcing Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector
notes.notes:
Wake up, Sleeper. No, you aren't dreaming! A little over a year from the launch of [b]Citizen Sleeper[/b], Jump Over the Age and Fellow Traveller are excited to announce [b]Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector[/b]!

We dropped the news today with an animated trailer, which introduces the game’s narrative set-up, plus a few of the key characters - the Sleeper, their colleague Serafin, and gang leader Laine.

[previewyoutube=tFOYaEQP9ks;full][/previewyoutube]

Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector places you in the role of a new sleeper - one who wasn’t as lucky to make it to relative comfort of Erlin’s Eye. Following a daring escape, you’ve made it all the way out to the Starward Belt, a remote asteroid cluster at the edge of the Helion System, only to have swapped one form of control for another. You’re now under the thumb of Laine, a notorious gang leader who provides you with Stabilizer - the drug your android body needs to survive - and uses it to exert control over you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/7e4f685c93ac159eda0387d235cefb702826734c.jpg[/img]
It’s a miserable existence for you and Serafin, your colleague in servitude. Together, you hatch a plan to escape. After a desperate attempt to free yourself by rewriting the very code that governs your system, you are on the run with a malfunctioning body, a price on your head and no memory of your past.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/5912162a39d00ba756f11c6b94e4813365a5517e.jpg[/img]
Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector reunites the very same core development team of solo developer Gareth Damian Martin, renowned comic book artist Guillaume Singelin, and celebrated composer, Amos Roddy. The game will take you to a new location, put you in the declining body of a new Sleeper, and once again ask you to build a life for yourself among the stars.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/72b6db788d81470e4edfe221a0d2dd5864b95d03.png[/img]
Citizen Sleeper’s acclaimed Tabletop RPG-inspired gameplay will also return in Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector alongside all new systems and mechanics that will offer more depth, complexity and challenge, as this time you'll have a ramshackle ship and a crew you’ve recruited, both of which need you to steer them through a system-wide crisis.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/249656c9e48c73a19f1c69b267d7de456fea93a3.png[/img]
There’s so much more for you out there, Sleeper. Eager to dive deeper into the Citizen Sleeper universe? Sign-up for the [url=https://jumpovertheage.substack.com/]Jump Over the Age Newsletter[/url], to get updates straight to your inbox. You’ll also receive The Helion Dispatches, a new series of narrative transmissions from the refugee ship, the Pilgrim Seed. 

So what are you waiting for? [url=https://jumpovertheage.substack.com/]Sign up right now![/url]

notes.title: Celebrating Tabletop Fest with a 30% discount and a blog about my inspirations!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/f54e0e4455ed2f6c10cbf83d3e768ce8af9cb3c5.png[/img]

Hi, this is Gareth Damian Martin, the developer and creator of Citizen Sleeper!

Citizen Sleeper is part of this week's Tabletop Fest and to celebrate I thought I would share a little more on the tabletop games that inspired me to make the game, and the ideas I borrowed to bring Elrin’s Eye to life.  

Obviously any game which features dice is most likely inspired by TTRPGs, but Citizen Sleeper is full of other features inspired by some of the most exciting games in the contemporary TTRPG scene.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/732bd9d57842c9b69131e62bec984874668a807d.png[/img]

First up is John Harper’s excellent TTRPG Blades in the Dark. Set in the dark fantasy city of Doskvol, Blades in the Dark focuses on high intensity heists, narrative-first gameplay and elegant and lightweight systems to simulate a whole city of criminal factions vying for control. One of the first tabletop games I ever ran as a game master, it immediately impressed me with its focus on “success at a cost” which gives its heists a fluid sense of escalation. Blades simulates the experience of being a master criminal always on the edge of failure, and so I found its balance of luck and strategy a good inspiration for modeling Citizen Sleeper’s sense of also living on the edge, not as a criminal, but as someone marginalized by society. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/aa1623b7bd81a0fe8ebc95bb71c2b08358101693.png[/img]

Blades in the Dark is also where I first encountered “clocks”, a simple way of tracking progress towards objectives, time passing, and upcoming events. I was really impressed by the utility and simplicity of this system and there’s nothing I love more as a GM than introducing a mysterious clock and ticking it up when the player fails a roll to give a sense of impending doom! So when it came to designing Citizen Sleeper I knew I wanted to use clocks to track everything from relationships to debts, something which also gives the game a unique TTRPG flavor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/5672dde2a6769112556a4657966b66fd1af92e17.png[/img]

Another part of Citizen Sleeper designed to feel very TTRPG is character progression. Rather than give out numerical XP in a traditional manner, I wanted character progression to reflect the players choices in the world, and to be a tool for letting the player figure out what they wanted to do next. Out of this came the idea of “drives” instead of “quests”, with the distinction being that Citizen Sleeper’s drives are all optional, and focus on the player's choice to engage or not engage with different parts of the world. I wanted players to choose their priorities, and then be rewarded for following through.

This kind of design is part of a wider movement in TTRPGs which began with the game Apocalypse World by D. Vincent Baker. First releasing in 2010 and going on to inspire a whole genre of TTRPGs under the label “Powered by the Apocalypse'', Apocalypse World focuses not on simulating everything that is happening the world, but instead abstracting ideas to simple dice systems so that the player has more agency and the game master is focused on driving the narrative, not adjudicating a complex rule set. This narrative-first kind of TTRPG is exactly what I hoped to emulate in Citizen Sleeper.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/9fb4bb03c728b51ade91717d354a8651ebf28f1c.png[/img]

Finally, one of the key inspirations for Citizen Sleeper comes from something that is a massive part of the contemporary TTRPG scene; actual play! For the uninitiated “actual play” is the term for video and audio content where players play TTRPGs live, telling stories that can change with a single dice roll. In particular Citizen Sleeper takes inspiration from one of the experimental and innovative actual play podcasts, Friends at the Table. Often telling richly diverse sci-fics stories with contemporary relevance, Friends at the Table’s brave approach was a huge inspiration for me. This counts double when it comes to the games 3 episode DLC sequence, which I wanted to have the story-telling rhythm of an actual play podcast, where the episodic story feels unpredictable and like something you discover as you play!

Whether I have achieved this goal will be decided when the final episode, episode: PURGE, launches on the 30th of  March. But however it turns out, it has been an exciting journey to bring some of the most interesting ideas from the contemporary TTRPG scene to video games, in some cases for the first time. I hope you’ve enjoyed it too, and if any of this has piqued your interest, I strongly recommend getting hold of a copy of a TTRPG mentioned above and trying to run a game with a few friends!

See you on the Eye!

Gareth

Since its launch in May earlier this year, Citizen Sleeper has been praised as “[i]a game that gets cyberpunk right[/i]”, with a deep narrative experience, unique tabletop RPG-inspired gameplay, compelling characters and a fascinating setting.

It’s been called “[i]one of the best games of the year[/i]” ([url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/jgmzzy/citizen-sleeper-review]VICE/Waypoint[/url]), “[i]an evocative life-sim RPG you won't want to wake up from[/i]” ([url=https://www.pcgamer.com/citizen-sleeper-review/]PC Gamer[/url]), and “[i]a game I'll be thinking about for years to come[/i]” ([url=https://www.gameinformer.com/review/citizen-sleeper/a-sleeper-hit]Game Informer[/url]). 

Recently, Citizen Sleeper has also been featured in numerous ‘Best of’ lists from the likes of [url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/our-favourite-games-of-2022-so-far#]Rock Paper Shotgun[/url], [url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/games/best-games-of-2022-so-far/]Paste[/url], [url=https://kotaku.com/best-video-games-2022-ps4-ps5-xbox-series-x-pc-switch-1848663025]Kotaku[/url] and [url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-top-100-pc-games-2022/]PC Gamer[/url].


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/e809809fe630e968a0d746f178684b31bddb448a.png[/img]

REFUGE is the second instalment in a three-episode arc, which will conclude in early 2023. It picks up right where the previous episode, FLUX left off. A strange event sends ripples through Erlin’s Eye. You will enter the refugee flotilla that arrived during FLUX to understand this new threat, and help the refugees stabilize their community.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/2989c1591cc0629cff6a1d2fa3d69c36df97cd87.png[/img]

In Episode: REFUGE, you will meet Sol, captain of the Pilgrim Seed, the biggest ship in the flotilla, and the refugees’ unofficial leader. Hailing from Ember’s Hearth, the largest moon of the gas giant Ember, Sol is a quiet pragmatist who is expected to shoulder some heavy responsibilities on behalf of the fractured flotilla.

Episode: REFUGE is available for [u][b]FREE[/b][/u] across all platforms for anyone who owns or or has access to Citizen Sleeper.

For those who don’t, great news -[b] Citizen Sleeper is on sale at 25% off[/b] (its highest discount ever) for the launch of Episode: REFUGE. Grab it now on Nintendo Switch, Steam, GOG, Epic, Humble, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One. It’s also available on Xbox Game Pass.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/482ff56f9b859dcd905624aadf426e7590bfd241.png[/img]

Citizen Sleeper has been compared favorably to the likes of Disco Elysium and Norco. What is even more remarkable about these comparisons is that Jump Over the Age, founded by Gareth Damian Martin (they/them), is a one-person game development studio. Gareth, along with Guillaume Singelin (character art) and Amos Roddy (music and sound) created Citizen Sleeper and they would love to hear your thoughts on the game, particularly these free episode updates!

Leave us a comment or a review on Steam, or whatever platform you use, and tweet your thoughts at [url=https://twitter.com/jumpovertheage]Jump Over the Age[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/fellowtravellr]Fellow Traveller[/url] with the hashtags #citizensleeper and #sleeperepisodes.

notes.title: One Week Until Launch
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/f2902759471b20d1404f45c612876014f3f4708d.jpg[/img]

We're only a week out from the release of Citizen Sleeper! Let's cover off the skills you'll need to consider before you begin the game, along with the strengths and weaknesses of each character class.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/9cd9469e8cef35672b590383a97a6ee57183a9c8.jpg[/img]

[b]ENGINEER:[/b] Work with machines and physical tools.
[b]INTERFACE:[/b] Work with digital interfaces.
[b]ENDURE:[/b] Use strength or strength of will.
[b]INTUIT:[/b] Approach problems with awareness.
[b]ENGAGE:[/b] Approach a problem head-on.


[b]THE OPERATOR[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/458dd533e156358ef3da9a50305a8d166cbc9d27.jpg[/img]
The Operator is the Sleeper who is closest to the digital world of emulated minds and AI protocols. Has a +1 to 'Interface'. Will certainly be helpful in hacking and gathering secrets. But with a -1 to 'Endure', in their weakened state you'll want to be careful with your choices.


[b]THE EXTRACTOR[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/4238f5a2694a9a1d70737505378e893999dcf850.jpg[/img]
Extractors are the Sleepers who, in particular, spend a lot of time alone in dangerous places. A good brute force option, with a +1 to 'Endure'. However, they often won't notice the bigger picture whilst problem solving, which could have consequences. Takes a hit to 'Intuit' with -1.


[b]THE MACHINIST[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379870/c9112ec74cb2dac57987f8eba6f5a77a6a8c9c38.jpg[/img]
Machinists are tinkerers, diligently keeping AI controlled tech and drones working in the field. A good option if you want to get your hands dirty with odd jobs from the start in the shipyard. Benefits from a +1 to 'Engineer', although suffers a -1 to 'Engage', which affects their ability to approach problems head on.

notes.title: Citizen Sleeper is a dystopian slice-of-life RPG on a space station
notes.notes:
It's the future and you're living on a space station in the great beyond! But the future is bad, and you're only a human consciousness in an failing artificial body owned by a corporation who want you back. That's how it goes in Citizen Sleeper, a sci-fi slice-of-life RPG announced this week by the creator of In Other Waters. I am certainly up for visiting a distant lawless space station to eek out a living, thwart a corp, and maybe even make some friends. Check out the announcement trailer below.
